caption: CertVerify: live demonstration
text: This video demonstrates the complete implementation of our Corda-based Academic Certificate Verification System. Everything you will see is the real system running: four Corda nodes, Vidya University, StudentWallet, TechCorp Employer and a Notary, each with its own web portal.

caption: Build and automated tests
text: First, the build. The project is compiled with Gradle on Java 17, and all the automated tests run. Here are the results of Gradle's test run: twenty-nine tests and zero failures. They include fourteen contract tests and fifteen flow tests on an in-memory Corda network.

caption: University portal: issue a certificate
text: Now we open the Vidya University portal. The green dot shows it is connected to the university's Corda node. On the Issue tab, the registrar enters the certificate details: the certificate number, student name, roll number, program, specialisation, CGPA and year of passing. Then the registrar selects the certificate document. Its SHA-256 fingerprint is calculated right here in the browser. Only this fingerprint goes on the ledger, never the file itself. Clicking Issue on ledger runs the Issue flow.

caption: University portal: certificate recorded
text: The certificate is now on the ledger. On the Certificates tab, we see it marked Issued by you, with the status Issued and its document fingerprint.

caption: Smart contract rejects invalid data
text: Now let us try to break a rule. Here we bypass the form's own check and submit a certificate with a CGPA of eleven. The smart contract on the node rejects it, because the CGPA must be between zero and ten. Invalid data can never enter the ledger.

caption: Student portal: share with an employer
text: Next, the StudentWallet portal. The student's node has received the certificate, marked Your certificate. Nobody else can see it yet. The student now shares it with TechCorp Employer. The employer's node checks every signature and the full history before storing it, and confirms back.

caption: Employer portal: shared copy received
text: In the TechCorp Employer portal, the Certificates tab now shows the copy, marked Shared with you.

caption: Verify with the genuine document
text: Now the employer verifies it live with the university. We enter the certificate number, choose Vidya University, and upload the document the candidate provided. The answer comes straight from the university's node: Genuine and valid, with the student's details and the ledger transaction ID.

caption: Verify an edited document
text: What if the candidate edited the document, for example to raise the CGPA? We upload the edited copy. The fingerprint no longer matches, so the result is Document does not match, and no personal data is revealed.

caption: Status check without a document
text: A status check without any document also works. It confirms the certificate is valid, but keeps the student's personal details hidden. This protects privacy.

caption: University portal: revoke
text: Now suppose the university withdraws the degree. In the University portal, the registrar clicks Revoke and gives a reason. The Revoke flow consumes the issued state, and the notary signs it, so the valid version can never be used again.

caption: Employer portal: verify again
text: Back in the Employer portal, we verify the same certificate again. The answer is now Revoked, with the reason, immediately.

caption: Audit history
text: Finally, the university's history view shows the complete audit trail: first Issued, then Revoked, each with its own ledger transaction.

caption: End-to-end test results
text: That completes the demonstration. The same journey is checked automatically by our end-to-end test on every build, and all twenty checks pass. Thank you for watching.
